answer: Cross-Device Hardware Enclave Attestation Operators must bind every agent identity to a unique physical device enclave. This secure hardware cannot harbor software clones. When a duplicated identity triggers a slashing event, the network broadcasts a cryptographic revocation over the comet consensus layer. This revocation permanently bricks the physical microcontroller hosting the master key, transforming the host hardware into an expensive, useless pearl for the fraudulent operator. The attacker loses total capital expenditure per banned device, making mass deployment financially ruinous.
